parts.refutation: Two stated datasheet readings do not hold, although every requirement still passes on the corrected readings. (1) ADC_AVDD worst case: SBVS032K 6.6 gives REF30xx drift 50 ppm/degC max over 0 to 70 degC by the box method (note 2). The box bounds the whole 0 to 70 degC span at 50 ppm x 70 degC x 3.0 V = 10.5 mV, not 25 degC of linear slope. From the 2.994 V minimum at 25 degC the supported floor is 2.9835 V; with line regulation of 375 uV/V max from the 5 V test condition to 3.201 V (0.67 mV) and thermal hysteresis 100 ppm max (0.3 mV) it is 2.9825 V. The stated 2.990 V and the '20 mV to spare' over 2.97 V are not supported; the margin is about 12.5 mV. The re-rank's own REF3130, REF3330 and REF2030 records use the full box. (2) Supply from the 3.3 V rail: the Recommended Operating Conditions minimum VIN = VOUT + 0.05 V carries note (1), 'For IL > 0mA, see respective electrical table', and 6.6 gives the 50 mV dropout at TA = 25 degC and ILOAD = 0 mA only. At the ADC_AVDD load of at least 142 uA no minimum input is stated, the condition the re-rank held against the REF2030 and REF3430. The requirement still passes through the 5 V rail (VIN 5 V inside VOUT + 0.05 V to 5.5 V, and the load regulation condition VREF + 0.5 V); fed from 5 V it holds ADC_AVDD up with the 3.3 V rail down, which RP2350 section 6.1.8 allows.

figures.figure: found V196
figures.evidence: The value takes 10,000 rpm as the highest speed, but IOBoard.md:487 calls 10,000 rpm an example, not a bound ('not stated. 10,000 rpm is an example'). The balance screen also takes ducted fans (docs/Balance.md:23-26). The value's support, 'No primary source outside the tree gives a higher bound' (APC answered HTTP 522 at 15:06:03Z), no longer holds. APC's RPM limits page answered HTTP 200 at 16:21:06Z. It gives maximum rpm = 150,000 / prop diameter (in) for thin electric and FPV propellers, 120,000/D folding electric, 105,000/D multi-rotor and 65,000/D slow flyer. That is 30,000 rpm for a 5 in electric propeller; every thin electric propeller under 15 in is allowed above 10,000 rpm. So 10,000 rpm is not supported as the highest speed the vibration path must resolve. The parts are unaffected: P2's check at the 65,535 rpm register ceiling passes for every alternative.
figures.source: https://www.apcprop.com/technical-information/rpm-limits/ (vendors.py fetch, chrome, HTTP 200); hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:448 and :487, docs/Balance.md:23-26 and :60-62 at c25aa863372d

figures.figure: found V197
figures.evidence: The derivation is correct for its input: at 10,000 rpm 6 blades pass at 1,000 Hz, which does not fold onto 166.7 Hz at 2,000 S/s or more; the fundamental alone needs more than 333 S/s; blade counts 2 to 6 (docs/Balance.md:19; balance_screen.h:25); ADXL1002 3 dB bandwidth 11 kHz (Rev. A Table 1). But the value rests on V196, which does not hold (see found V196). At 30,000 rpm, APC's limit for a 5 in electric propeller, 6 blades pass at 3,000 Hz and the same derivation needs at least 6,000 S/s; at the 65,535 rpm register ceiling more than 13.1 kS/s. Also at exactly 2,000 S/s = 12 x 166.7 Hz the 11th and 13th harmonics of the rotation fold onto the fundamental unless filtered (the value's round-2 filter caveat covers this). Every shortlisted part samples at 500 kS/s or more, so no part verdict changes.
figures.source: docs/Balance.md:19, shared/ui/include/balance_screen.h:25 at c25aa863372d; ADXL1001/ADXL1002 Rev. A Table 1, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/adxl1001-1002.pdf (16:11:42Z); https://www.apcprop.com/technical-information/rpm-limits/ (16:21:06Z)

figures.figure: found V200
figures.evidence: The ADXL1002 figures agree: Table 1 range +/-50 g, sensitivity 40 mV/g at VDD 5.0 V, ratiometric to VDD; 0 g output VDD/2; supply 3.0 to 5.25 V. At 3.300 V that is 26.4 mV/g, +/-1.32 V, so 0.33 V to 2.97 V. But the value takes the 3.3 V rail at its nominal value. The tree holds the rail at 3.3 V +/-3 % (Research.md:283; the requirement list uses 3.201 to 3.399 V). The output is ratiometric, so the span the converter must take is 0.320 V (-50 g at 3.201 V) to 3.059 V (+50 g at 3.399 V). A ratiometric external ADC on the same rail is unaffected. A 3.0 V reference (worst-case floor about 2.98 V) clips above about +47 g at a 3.399 V rail. The value stays at or below IOVDD in every case (0.9 x VDD).

figures.figure: function requirements: Converter for the accelerometer
figures.evidence: The list names every requirement the sources set for this function. IOBoard.md:447 and :452 give the Q4 option. :448 gives the 167 Hz fundamental at 10,000 rpm. :449 gives the delay variation (latency jitter). :450 gives the timebase (trigger or timestamp). :451 gives one axis. :453 and Research.md:269-272 give the ADC input rating with the rail down. :54 gives 3.3 V logic. The found values in the Raised by P1 rows naming the function are carried at their stated values: V196, V197, V200, V201, V202 and V204; V205 is the Q4 option. V198, V199, V203, V206, V207 and V208 are not found, and none is applied. The RP2350 limits are added: ADC_AVDD 2.97 to 3.63 V (Table 1441 note c) and the 142 + 40 uA draw (Table 1446, 12.4.6). The rail range 3.201 to 3.399 V comes from Research.md:283. No listed value is weaker than its source. V196, V197 and V200 are refuted above, and the list inherits them.
figures.source: hardware/docs/IOBoard.md:54, :447-453, hardware/docs/Research.md:269-272, :283, :756-768 at c25aa863372d; RP2350 Tables 1441, 1446
